newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Liberals headed for landslide - poll.
newsitem.headline: Canada Liberals headed for landslide - poll.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien and the Liberal party are poised for a landslide victory potentially greater than the one that brought them to power in 1993, a poll published on Wednesday showed.
The Financial Post/Compas poll showed the Liberals have the support of 47 percent of decided voters ahead of a federal election on June 2, the Financial Post newspaper said.
It said the Conservatives have 18 percent of support, Reform 13 percent, the New Democratic Party (NDP) 10 percent and the Bloc Quebecois 11 percent.
Of the 2,600 people surveyed, 23 percent said they were undecided.
The poll was conducted from April 15 to 25 and has a margin of error of plus or minus 1.9 percent, 19 times out of 20, the newspaper said.
It said Liberal support comes largely at the expense of the NDP, which is slipping in its traditional strongholds in the western provinces of British Columbia and Saskatchewan.
The Conservatives, led by Jean Charest, are gaining ground on the Bloc in Quebec, which may even lose its status as the official opposition, Compas pollster Chris Martyn said.
In 1993, the Liberals won 177 seats in the House of Parliament with 41.3 percent of the total vote.
